//: Copy this file to config.json and edit. Everything the VS layer touches is described here.

tls.//: Optional and additive. HTTP on 'port' always stays up for the Wall Players (mpv reads the camera relay) and Quandary webhooks. Turning this on ADDS an HTTPS listener on 'httpsPort' for the tables - a secure origin means the camera works with no Chrome flags. Make a trusted cert with: ./install-linux.sh cert --host 192.168.1.20

quandary.//comment: Quandary Control is never modified. We connect as a GM socket client and use its public REST API.

rules.//armedOnly: true = teams can only earn/fire sabotages while the operator (or Quandary) has armed the match.
rules.//difficulty: easy | normal | hard. Scales every mini-game's win and lose thresholds. 'normal' is each game exactly as it was tuned. Set from the operator Settings screen; applies without a restart.
rules.//minigames: Pool the server draws from at random. Remove ids to disable a game.
rules.//avoidRepeatCount: Don't hand a team the same game again until N other games have been played.

A.name: Room A
A.//quandaryRoomId: The room UUID from Quandary Control (see Admin > room, or GET /api/v1/rooms).

wallPlayer.//token: Must match vsToken in the Wall Player's config.json.
wallPlayer.//sabotageVideos: Optional filenames from the Wall Player video folder used by the 'takeover' sabotage.

lights.//driver: null | kasa | shelly | hue | hass | webhook
lights.//devices: kasa/shelly: IP addresses. hue: light ids. hass: entity_ids. webhook: ignored.

camera.//label: Optional substring of the USB camera's device label, if the PC has more than one camera.

options.//: TP-Link Kasa plugs/bulbs, local LAN protocol on port 9999. No cloud, no dependencies.
